description: A common ESP32 dev board (Xtensa dual-core, Wi-Fi + Bluetooth). Legs are labeled by silkscreen (D2, D4, ... VP, VN), not by raw GPIO number.
how_to_use: VN/VP/D34/D35 are input-only (no output driver, no internal pull resistors) — real hardware, not a lesson-specific restriction. Peripherals (I2C, SPI, UART) can each be mapped to nearly any GPIO in software (the ESP32's GPIO matrix), so no bus pin is hardware-fixed the way it is on an AVR board — only RX0/TX0 (UART0, used for USB flashing/Serial Monitor) are excluded by default, for the same reason as the Uno's pins 0/1.

plain.what: A board with Wi-Fi and Bluetooth built in — for projects that talk to your phone or the internet.
plain.how: Program it like an Arduino over USB. It runs at 3.3 V, so be careful with 5 V parts. The silver box is the Wi-Fi radio.
